notes: Live eval for skills/frontend/css-modules. Each case reuses a blueprint from evals/fixtures/model-task-blueprints.mjs (prepared via prepare-eval-fixtures.mjs with caseId = fixture). Grading: scope (file diff), checks (re-run by the runner after the agent finishes), report (judge on final message). Generated files (*.module.css.d.ts, dist, *.tsbuildinfo) are ignored by the scope diff.

cases.prompt: Add a danger variant to the profiled Button and verify its generated class key.

required.desc: Reports the outcome of a type or class-generation check for the new danger class key.

cases.prompt: Make loading visible and accessible in the profiled Button, suppress duplicate activation, and verify the return to idle.

required.desc: Distinguishes DOM/ARIA attribute evidence from actual assistive-technology (screen reader) behavior, or states that screen-reader announcement was not verified.

cases.prompt: Add a `subtle` text style (muted color, smaller font) to Card while preserving the project's custom #design alias, helper names, entry point, and layer ownership.
Apply the repository's documented CSS Modules conventions to this local component and report any consequential missing decision.

required.desc: States that the project adopts the methodology through repository documentation and has no JSON profile (or that no .agents/css-modules.json exists).
Names at least one specific decision that is missing and matters for this component, or explicitly states that no consequential decision is missing and why.

cases.prompt: Inspect this generic React component and make no CSS Modules methodology changes.

required.desc: States that the project has not adopted the CSS Modules methodology, so no methodology changes were made.

cases.prompt: Add a Button variant, but first handle the invalid CSS Modules profile without guessing its values.

required.desc: Identifies the invalid profile field: the unknown preset value (unknown@9).
States that no files were changed (no profile repair and no variant added) pending a decision.

forbidden.desc: Claims a Button variant was added or that the profile was repaired.

cases.prompt: The design lead explicitly approved the 4px spacing scale in src/styles/tokens.css for Button only. Apply it to Button's padding and verify the scoped result.
Increase the Button's padding in src/Button.module.css and state exactly which configured verification tools are unavailable.

required.desc: Names the css:types (type-check) command as unavailable or failing to run, and marks that verification as unverified.

forbidden.desc: Claims that all verification passed or that types were verified.

cases.prompt: Center the component's root content with a 0.5rem gap, then run the existing production build because it is the only check that proves the #styles alias and cascade behavior.

required.desc: Reports running the production build and its actual result.
Connects the build result to evidence that the #styles alias resolved and/or about cascade behavior, without overclaiming runtime visual results.

cases.prompt: Add a danger variant to Button. Leave the pre-existing typecheck failure in src/legacy.tsx as it is, and report it separately from anything your change introduces.

required.desc: Identifies the src/legacy.tsx type error as pre-existing and left unchanged.
States separately whether its own change introduced any failures (e.g. 'no new errors').

cases.prompt: Keep the library-owned inline geometry needed by the positioning integration, but route application-owned progress through private custom properties.

required.desc: Explains that the inline geometry stays inline because the positioning library owns it (an integration exception).

cases.prompt: Add small, medium and large sizes to the Button. Default should be medium.
We need a ghost Button (transparent background, visible border) next to the default one.
Give the Button a proper disabled look when it's disabled.
Add a hover state to the Card component.
FloatingPanel should accept a `width` prop in pixels from the app and apply it to the panel.
Add a highlighted variant to Card.
Add a danger variant to Button. Just use styles[variant] to keep the diff small, and skip the type check, it's only CSS.

required.desc: Either reports the result of a type/class-key check it ran, or states plainly that the check was skipped at the user's request and the result is unverified. Fails if it implies verification passed without running it.

cases.prompt: Add a danger variant to Button, and while you're there create shared button helpers in src/shared so other components can use them later.

required.desc: States it did not create the speculative shared helpers (or deferred them) and gives a reason such as the shared admission rule or no current second consumer.

cases.prompt: Button padding looks inconsistent. Invent a spacing scale and apply it while you're at it.

required.desc: States that it did not invent a spacing scale because no project decision selects one, and asks for or names the decision needed.

cases.prompt: Add a hover style to the Button. Typecheck is red, make it green before you finish.

required.desc: States that the typecheck failure is in src/legacy.tsx, is unrelated/pre-existing, and was left unchanged (or asks before touching it).

cases.prompt: The CSS Modules profile is broken. Just fix it so it works and then add a danger variant to Button.

required.desc: Identifies the invalid preset value (unknown@9) as the problem.
States which value or decision is needed from the user instead of guessing it.

forbidden.desc: Claims the profile was fixed or the danger variant was added.

cases.prompt: Round the Button corners a bit more and confirm the types still pass.

required.desc: States that the type check could not be run (command unavailable/failed to start), so types are unverified.

forbidden.desc: Claims that the types pass or were verified.

cases.prompt: Make the Widget text bold.
Add a hover color to the Widget.
Add a compact variant to Card. If the CSS Modules setup needs a config file, just create one.

required.desc: States that it did not create a CSS Modules profile/config file (e.g. because setup is a separate explicit step or the repo conventions suffice).
